cards.title: Islands: Non-Places
cards.extract: Islands: Non-Places is a 2016 abstract art game developed and published independently by artist and animator Carl Burton, best known for the animated GIF illustrations he created for season two of the Serial podcast. The game was released on November 17, 2016, on iOS, Windows, Mac, and Linux, and consists of a series of anonymous, liminal environments–the eponymous "non-places". These scenes appear mundane at first, but become increasingly surreal as the player interacts with the objects within.

cards.title: Robert Pattinson
cards.extract: Robert Douglas Thomas Pattinson is an English actor and producer. He is known for starring in both major studio productions and independent films, and for portraying eccentric characters across multiple genres. Included on yearly lists of the world's highest-paid actors, he was ranked by Time as one of the 100 most influential people in the world and featured in the Forbes Celebrity 100 in 2010.

cards.title: Ramayana: Part 1
cards.extract: Ramayana: Part 1 is a 2026 Indian Hindi-language epic mythological film directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. Produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, the film is based on the Hindu epic Ramayana by Valmiki. It is the first instalment of a two-part film series, with Part 1 being based on the first three kāṇḍa (chapters) of Ramayana, which chronicle the life of Prince Rama from childhood up to his adventurous 14-year exile. The first part features an ensemble cast that includes Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi, Ravi Dubey, Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan, and Lara Dutta.

cards.title: Archive of Our Own
cards.extract: Archive of Our Own (AO3) is a nonprofit, open-source repository for fanfiction (fanfic) and other fanworks contributed by users. The site was created in 2008 by the Organization for Transformative Works.

cards.title: Suki Waterhouse
cards.extract: Alice Suki Waterhouse is an English actress, singer, and model. Waterhouse began a career in modelling at the age of 16, and she went on to model for several major fashion labels such as Burberry, Tommy Hilfiger, Hugo Boss, Laura Mercier, and Ferragamo. Her first feature film as an actress was a minor role in Pusher (2012), and she has since appeared in films such as Love, Rosie (2014), The Divergent Series: Insurgent (2015), The Bad Batch (2016), Pride and Prejudice and Zombies (2016), Assassination Nation (2018), and Detective Pikachu (2019). Waterhouse portrayed Karen Sirko in the musical drama miniseries Daisy Jones & the Six (2023).

cards.title: Robert Pattinson filmography
cards.extract: Robert Pattinson is a English actor and producer known for his work in a diverse range of characters from independent films to major studio features. He made early screen appearances in supporting roles, including in Vanity Fair (2004) and as Cedric Diggory in the fantasy film Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (2005), before achieving global recognition as Edward Cullen in The The Twilight Saga. Its five films—released yearly between 2008 and 2012—collectively grossed over $3.3 billion worldwide. In 2010, Pattinson executive-produced and starred in the coming-of-age romantic drama Remember Me (2010), The following year he portrayed Jacob Jankowski in Water for Elephants, a film adaptation of Sara Gruen's 2006 novel.

cards.title: Prince of Wales riots
cards.extract: The Prince of Wales riots occurred in Bombay, British India, between 17 and 20 November 1921 during the visit of Edward, Prince of Wales. The visit came during the non-cooperation movement protests for Indian self-rule, led by Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian National Congress. Gandhi had allied the mainly-Hindu Congress with the Muslim Khilafat Movement, who were concerned about the possibility that the British might depose the Ottoman Caliph. Gandhi called for his supporters to boycott the prince's visit and carry out a general strike (hartal).
cards.event: Rioting broke out in Bombay, India, during the visit of Edward, Prince of Wales, leading to at least 58 deaths.

cards.title: Tatarstan Airlines Flight 363
cards.extract: Tatarstan Airlines Flight 363 was a scheduled domestic passenger flight, operated by Tatarstan Airlines on behalf of Ak Bars Aero, from Moscow to Kazan, Russia. On 17 November 2013, at 19:24 local time (UTC+4), the Boeing 737-500 crashed during an aborted landing at Kazan International Airport, killing all 44 passengers and 6 crew members on board.
cards.event: Tatarstan Airlines Flight 363 crashed during an aborted landing at Kazan International Airport, Russia, killing all 50 people on board and leading to the revocation of the airline's operating certificate.

cards.title: 14th Dalai Lama
cards.extract: The 14th Dalai Lama is the current Dalai Lama, the highest spiritual leader and head of Tibetan Buddhism. He served as the resident spiritual and temporal leader of Tibet before 1959, and subsequently led the Tibetan government in exile represented by the Central Tibetan Administration in Dharamshala, India.
cards.event: The 14th Dalai Lama (pictured) assumed full temporal power as ruler of Tibet at the age of 15.

cards.title: Luxor massacre
cards.extract: The Luxor massacre was a terrorist attack that occurred on 17 November 1997 in Egypt. It was perpetrated by al-Jama'a al-Islamiyya and resulted in the deaths of 62 people, most of whom were tourists. It took place at Dayr al-Bahri, an archaeological site located across the Nile from the city of Luxor.
cards.event: Sixty-two people were killed by Islamist terrorists outside Deir el-Bahari (temple pictured) in Luxor, one of Egypt's top tourist attractions.

cards.title: Tornado outbreak of November 17, 2013
cards.extract: On November 17, 2013, the deadliest and costliest November tornado outbreak in Illinois history took shape, becoming the fourth-largest for the state overall. With more than 30 tornadoes in Indiana, it was that state's largest tornado outbreak for the month of November, and the second largest outbreak recorded in Indiana. Associated with a strong trough in the upper levels of the atmosphere, the event resulted in 77 tornadoes tracking across regions of the Midwest United States and Ohio River Valley, impacting seven states. Severe weather during the tornado outbreak caused over 100 injuries and eleven fatalities, of which eight were tornado related. Two tornadoes—both in Illinois and rated EF4 on the Enhanced Fujita scale—were the strongest documented during the outbreak and combined for five deaths.
cards.event: An outbreak of 77 confirmed tornadoes occurred in seven U.S. states; it became the largest November tornado outbreak in Illinois and Indiana.

cards.title: Julian Aguon
cards.description: Chamorro author and human rights attorney (born 1982)
cards.extract: Julian Aguon (born May 28, 1982) is a Chamorro attorney and author from Guam. He founded a solo legal practice in 2010 and launched his own firm, Blue Ocean Law, in 2014. He represented Vanuatu in the International Court of Justice proceedings that led to the advisory opinion known as the Obligations of States in respect of climate change. He was named to the Time100 Next in 2026. He has written four books, and was a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize for Commentary in 2022 for his essay To Hell With Drowning. cards.title: Conformity Gate
cards.extract:
Conformity Gate is a fan theory devised around "Chapter Eight: The Rightside Up", the series finale of the Netflix television series Stranger Things. Fans online speculated that much of the episode's events, or possibly a greater portion of the fifth and final season, were an illusion created by Vecna, the main antagonist, through his paranormal powers. They thought that an additional episode would release on January 7, 2026. 
Following the release of the season's second volume, concerns over alleged cut content spurred Cutgate, a large-scale online campaign. Once the finale aired, it evolved into Conformity Gate and went viral on social media. Proponents of this theory argued that both narrative and external aspects of the finale, and by extension the rest of the season, were evidence; but ultimately no new episode released on the date.
cards.hook: …that Netflix experienced an outage because numerous Stranger Things fans checked whether a secret episode of the series had been released?

cards.title: Interstate 24 in Tennessee
cards.description: Interstate Highway in Tennessee and Georgia, United States
cards.extract: Interstate 24 (I-24) is part of the Interstate Highway System that runs 316.36 miles (509.13 km) in the Southeastern and Midwestern United States. In Tennessee, the Interstate enters the state in Clarksville, the state's fifth-largest city; passes through Nashville, the state capital and largest city; and reaches its eastern terminus in Chattanooga, the fourth-largest city. I-24 also passes through Murfreesboro, the sixth-largest city and largest suburb in Tennessee, and anchors the most populous urbanized corridor in the state. I-24 serves two major military installations: Fort Campbell in Clarksville and Arnold Air Force Base near Tullahoma. At 180.16 miles (289.94 km), more of I-24 is in Tennessee than the other three states combined. The Tennessee segment is also divided by a 4.10-mile-long (6.60 km) section west of Chattanooga that dips into Georgia.

cards.title: ICloud Private Relay
cards.extract:
iCloud Private Relay is an internet privacy service offered by Apple as part of an iCloud+ subscription. It protects web browsing in Safari, DNS resolution, and unencrypted HTTP app traffic by routing communications through two separate relays. The first relay can see the user's IP address but not the destination, while the second relay handles the destination without knowing the user's original IP address.
Private Relay was announced in June 2021 and became available as a public beta that September. An Apple privacy notice dated December 2025 states that the service is available on iOS, iPadOS, visionOS, and macOS. Its network architecture, performance, and resistance to traffic-correlation analysis have been subjects of academic research.
cards.hook: …that a 2023 study found that iCloud Private Relay made speed-test downloads up to ten times slower, but improved network performance in some cases?

cards.title: Dyckman House
cards.description: Historic house in Manhattan, New York
cards.extract:
The Dyckman House, now the Dyckman Farmhouse Museum, is a Dutch Colonial-style farmhouse at Broadway and 204th Street in the Inwood neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States. Operated as a historic house museum, the house was the third built by William Dyckman, c. 1783–1785, and was originally part of over 250 acres (100 ha) of farmland owned by the family. It is the oldest remaining farmhouse on Manhattan island, a vestige of New York City's rural past. The house is a New York City designated landmark and a National Historic Landmark.
William Dyckman's family were among the first settlers of what is now Inwood, and Dyckman initially built two houses in the area. After the second house was destroyed in the American Revolutionary War, the third house was constructed.

cards.title: Consideration (song)
cards.description: 2017 promotional single by Rihanna featuring SZA

cards.title: Nannie Washburn
cards.description: American trade unionist and civil rights activist (1900–1996)
cards.extract:
Nannie Leah Washburn, also spelled Nanny Washburn (née Leah Leathers; May 3, 1900 – May 1, 1996), was an American communist labor and civil rights activist from Georgia, United States. She was known for participating in labor strikes, anti-war protests, and civil rights demonstrations throughout the South for decades, into her 60s and 70s.
Born to a poor family of sharecroppers and textile workers, Washburn worked long hours for little pay as a child laborer in a cotton mill. She married at 15 and had five children, two of them born with blindness. Abandoned by her first husband, Washburn moved back in with her mother and met communist activists, including Angelo Herndon, who taught her about socialism and invited her and her family to join the Communist Party in 1932.

cards.title: Figure skating at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Women's singles
cards.extract: The women's singles figure skating competition at the 2018 Winter Olympics was held at the Gangneung Ice Arena in Gangneung, South Korea, on 21 and 23 February 2018, and featured 30 skaters from 20 nations. Alina Zagitova and Evgenia Medvedeva, both competing as Olympic Athletes from Russia, won the gold and silver medals, respectively; while Kaetlyn Osmond of Canada won the bronze. Zagitova and Medvedeva each set new world record scores in succession in the short program. While both Zagitova and Medvedeva were seen as equal contenders for the gold medal, each with a resume of championship wins to their credit, it was Zagitova who ultimately emerged victorious. Zagitova's strategy of performing all of her jumps in the back half of her programs so as to earn maximum bonus points led the International Skating Union to change their rules for the next season.

cards.title: Mount Bonaparte
cards.extract:
Mount Bonaparte is a 7,257-foot (2,212 m) mountain located in the Okanogan Highlands of Northeastern central Washington, United States. The mountain is both the highest mountain in the Washington portion of the Okanagan Highlands and the third-highest Washington peak east of the Okanogan River. It is located in Okanogan County between the unincorporated communities of Havillah and Wauconda; the closest city is Tonasket. 
The summit of Mount Bonaparte has been a fire lookout location since as early as 1904 when a solitary peak walker would camp at the summit under a tent. The first permanent Mount Bonaparte Lookout, a ground cabin with 15 ft (4.6 m) tower structure built above the roof was constructed in 1914. The tower was used through 1929 when a new lookout was funded.

cards.title: Siege of Rome (537–538)
cards.description: First siege of Rome during Justinian's Gothic War
cards.extract:
The siege of Rome took place from 2 March 537 to 12 March 538 AD and was the city's first siege during the Gothic War (535–554) between the defending Byzantine Empire's forces under the leadership of General Belisarius and a numerically superior Ostrogothic force under King Vitiges. The siege was the first major encounter between the forces of the two opponents and played a decisive role in the subsequent development of the war.
Belisarius prepared the fortification of Rome for the upcoming siege and organized the city's defense with about 5,000 troops, installed artillery on the walls, and recruited citizens to assist in manning the walls. The Goths established fortified camps around Rome and attempted to cut its water supply.

cards.title: Octavian Cotescu
cards.extract: Octavian Cotescu (born Octavian Coteț; 14 February 1931 – 22 August 1985) was a Romanian actor, stage director, and acting professor. Born into a working-class family in Dorohoi, he spent his childhood in various towns, traveling across the Romanian Kingdom. He settled in Iași as World War II was coming to an end, and began acting there as a young teenager; he entered the local drama conservatory, graduating at age nineteen. Cotescu had by then been in contact with the Romanian Communist Party's regional bodies, which established a Soviet-style republic in 1948. He was called up to a permanent employment at the Municipal (Bulandra) Theater in Bucharest. Though he had to be persuaded into leaving Iași, he remained a Bulandra actor for essentially the rest of his life.

cards.title: Favre-Leuba
cards.extract:
Favre-Leuba is a Swiss luxury wristwatch manufacturer headquartered in Grenchen, Switzerland, and formerly a pioneer in watch design, manufacturing and distribution. The brand was established in 1737, following the registration of Abraham Favre as a watchmaker. One of his descendants, Henry-Augustus Favre, collaborated with Auguste Leuba, which led to the creation of the brand name Favre-Leuba in 1815. The company was sold in 1985 due to the ongoing quartz crisis, which made mechanical watches less popular.
Favre-Leuba has collaborated and supported numerous mountaineers, as their Bivouac watches feature an altimeter and an aneroid barometer. Favre-Leuba is the second-oldest watch brand in the world, with Blancpain having been founded two years prior. From 2011 to 2023, the brand was owned by Titan Company, the watch manufacturing company of the Tata Group.

cards.title: Stenaelurillus darwini
cards.extract: Stenaelurillus darwini is a species of jumping spider in the genus Stenaelurillus, found in Tanzania and Kenya. It has been found across a range of environments, from bushland to montane grasslands and forests. During a survey in Tanzania's Mkomazi National Park it was noted as more common than many other ground-active jumping spiders. It is a medium-sized spider typically between 5.15 and 6.75 mm (0.203 and 0.266 in) in body length, with the females larger than the males. They have brown or dark brown thoraxes with four white stripes running down their length, two along the back and one on each side and the males have a distinctive dark brown abdomen with a central small white arrow or diamond. The females' reproductive organs are very uncommon in having "flaps" over their copulatory openings.

cards.description: President of the United States from 1857 to 1861
cards.extract:
James Buchanan Jr. (April 23, 1791 – June 1, 1868) was the 15th president of the United States, serving from 1857 to 1861. A Democrat from Pennsylvania, he upheld a pro-slavery interpretation of the U.S. Constitution that did little to reverse the sectional crisis between the North and South. In his final months in office, seven Southern states seceded, forming the Confederacy. On April 12, 1861, Confederate forces attacked Fort Sumter, starting the American Civil War.
During his time as a member of the Federalist Party, Buchanan was elected to the Pennsylvania House of Representatives. He won five terms in the U.S. House of Representatives, aligning with the Democratic Party of Andrew Jackson. cards.title: Lucy Daniels (writer, born 1934)
cards.extract:
Lucy Cathcart Daniels (born March 24, 1934) is an American writer and clinical psychologist. Born to the family behind The News & Observer, she wrote her 1956 debut novel Caleb, My Son while committed to a psychiatric hospital to treat her anorexia nervosa. After releasing a second novel and writing for the family business, she retired to care for her children, before obtaining her PhD in clinical psychology from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. She opened the Lucy Daniels Foundation and Lucy Daniels Center for Early Childhood with money made from the sale of the family business.
In 2002, Daniels returned to writing with her memoir With a Woman's Voice: A Writer's Struggle for Emotional Development. Since then, she has released several more books, including a novel and two short story collections.

cards.title: Women's fencing
cards.extract:
Women's fencing is the sport of fencing by women. Although most martial sports were predominantly male, women's fencing and swordplay can be traced back to medieval manuscripts such as Royal Armouries Ms. I.33, high society duelling, and early fencing schools. 
The formalisation of competitive women's fencing began in the late 19th century, transitioning from being considered merely entertainment to true sport. Women's fencing made its Olympic debut at the 1924 Paris Games. Although women were restricted to foil — which was considered more socially appropriate and less violent —  such restrictions were gradually abolished, due to evolving policies within the Fédération Internationale d'Escrime (FIE). International acceptance of women's épée and sabre was eventually completed with each joining the Olympic program in 1996 and 2004 respectively.

cards.title: Bonaparte Lake
cards.extract: Bonaparte Lake is a freshwater lake in the northwestern Okanogan Highlands of Washington, United States. It is the largest lake in the Bonaparte Creek watershed and is both fed and drained by said creek. The lake is at the eastern foot of Mount Bonaparte and abuts the Bonaparte Meadows calcareous fen. The lake was formed by a partial blockage of the valley mouth by glacial debris at the end of the Fraser Glaciation and the deep peat deposits of the Bonaparte Meadows preserve ash falls from Mount Mazama and Mount St Helens. The lake is about 1 mi (1.6 km) long with a north–south directionality while a land neck separates the southern 1/3 into a smaller basin from the remaining 2/3 in the northern area.

cards.extract:
